surveyDefinition.title: Video Streaming Subscriptions — consumer survey (Latin America)
surveyDefinition.whatThisSurveyIs: A business-to-consumer (B2C) market research questionnaire about Video Streaming Subscriptions. Every question asks about Video Streaming Subscriptions specifically — not the wider market, not adjacent categories, and not any named brand. It is designed to tell a client what buyers in Latin America actually do and want in this category.
surveyDefinition.whoseContextThisIs: Adults in Latin America who buy or use Video Streaming Subscriptions for personal or household use. Respondents qualify if they: Currently has an active paid subscription to at least one video streaming service (e.g., Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max, etc.); Primary decision-maker or co-decision-maker for household streaming subscriptions; Aged 18 or older; Able to complete an online survey in the relevant language. Excluded: Individuals who only use free ad-supported streaming (e.g., free tier of Pluto TV, YouTube without subscription); Businesses or institutions purchasing streaming for commercial use (e.g., bars, hotels, offices); Cable/satellite TV subscribers who do not also have a streaming subscription; Children under 18 (unless surveyed via parent proxy, which is out of scope for this consumer survey).
surveyDefinition.whyTheseRespondents: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
respondentBehaviours: Streams video content at least weekly
Subscribes to one or more paid streaming services
Engages with original content and on-demand viewing
May churn or rotate subscriptions based on content library
whatIsDeliberatelyNotAsked: Age or household income — these define who was recruited, not what is measured, so they appear in the audience definition rather than as questions.
Brand, company or manufacturer names — the survey stays at category level so findings are not tied to one competitor set.
Where the respondent lives — region is chosen when viewing the results, so asking it again would waste a question.
surveyDefinition.howToReadTheNumbers: Percentages are simulated from a persona-weighted panel of 2,500 synthetic respondents built from real market evidence, not from fieldwork. Single-choice, ranking and rating-scale questions sum to 100%. Multi-select questions do not — each option is an independent share of respondents choosing it. The N shown on each question is the display base for that item.

structure.storyline: Questions run in a planned narrative order: broad and easy first, specific and sensitive last.
structure.storylineSummary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming—whether they subscribe, how often and in what contexts they watch, who in the household is involved, and the underlying motivations. It then moves into the purchase journey: what triggers a subscription, how they discover and compare services, where they subscribe, how often they review or rotate, what they spend, and what drives their choice. metadata.storyline_summary: The survey opens by establishing the respondent's relationship with video streaming—whether they subscribe, how often and in what contexts they watch, who in the household is involved, and the underlying motivations. It then moves into the purchase journey: what triggers a subscription, how they discover and compare services, where they subscribe, how often they review or rotate, what they spend, and what drives their choice. Next, it explores their expectations and preferences: must-have features, quality cues, subscription formats, content claims, trade-offs, and value expectations. Finally,
storyline_notes: For a subscription category, the canonical 'purchase_cycle' was reframed as 'subscription_cycle' to capture review/renewal/rotation rather than restock frequency.
Added a 'subscription_routine' beat to capture the habitual vs. reconsidered nature of subscription decisions, which is key for churn-prone streaming.
In preferences, 'format_packaging' was adapted to 'subscription_format' to cover plan types (monthly/annual, ad-supported, multi-profile) instead of physical packaging.
In consumer_profile, 'usage_occasion' and 'usage_frequency' were kept but tailored to viewing occasions and weekly streaming intensity.
For Latin America, the discovery and channel beats emphasize mobile-first and carrier/bundle channels, reflecting high mobile usage and common carrier billing in the region.
Spend bands and value expectations are designed to be sensitive to lower average income and high price sensitivity in the region.
metadata.classification_reason: Video streaming subscriptions are purchased by individual consumers and households for personal entertainment use. While some business plans exist, the dominant and defining market is consumer subscription services (e.g., Netflix, Disney+, Hulu).
